title: Two interfaces, one class
description:
Inheriting from several **interfaces** is the safe, common use of multiple inheritance: the class simply promises to do several things.

Two interfaces are provided. Write `class Duck : public IFlyer, public ISwimmer` that implements both (`fly()` returns `"flaps"`, `swim()` returns `"paddles"`). Then write the two free functions, each of which accepts anything with the right ability:

- `std::string takeOff(const IFlyer& flyer)` returns `"up: "` plus what the flyer does,
- `std::string dive(const ISwimmer& swimmer)` returns `"down: "` plus what the swimmer does.
lessonTitle: Multiple Inheritance and Virtual Base Classes
